key_insight: Stratified turbulence can produce rare but very strong local buoyancy-flux bursts, with transport intermittency growing nonlinearly with buoyancy Reynolds number and persisting even under stable stratification.
engineering_relevance: For atmospheric and ocean modeling, these results imply that mixing and vertical transport may be dominated by intermittent burst events, so parameterizations should account for non-Gaussian extremes rather than only mean fluxes.
method: Direct numerical simulations of the Boussinesq equations
Large parametric sweep over Froude number (0.01–1) for Pr = 1 and 6
Analysis of buoyancy flux, mixing efficiency, shear parameters, and vertical momentum flux
evidence_signal: Across the simulated regimes, buoyancy-flux statistics show very heavy tails (kurtosis up to ~10^2), with skewness increasing roughly as a power law in buoyancy Reynolds number and the domain-averaged flux following distinct scaling trends.
watch_item: The conclusions come from idealized DNS and may not transfer directly to full geophysical settings without accounting for rotation, boundaries, and more complex forcing.
paper_title: Scaling laws and local enhancements of buoyancy flux in stratified turbulent flows
